In the game a new player now reads 5 short lines over it, in about 26 seconds: a tap moves to the next line, and Skip stays. Our mission is to help people earn by taking part, even while they rest, and to build the platform that keeps people in the work as AI learns it. Everything on the next nine slides is in this picture: people give the blocks, agents make the connections. Today we show that potential with play money.

Now AI is learning the work too: almost 40 percent of jobs worldwide are exposed to it (IMF, 2024). What AI cannot make is you: your own choices. BYT is built on that.

This is the why now. When work changes, people need a way to earn from what only they have. For a buyer it is the same fact: a model can guess the crowd, so the scarce thing is a checked answer from a real person who said yes.

What BYT is

You own a tested digital version of how you choose. It earns for you.

1. Play

A minute of taps. Each tap is one block of your Sym.

2. Prove

Code tests your Sym against you. Nothing is taken on trust.

3. Earn

It answers for you while you rest. You check it, then you are paid.

We call it a Sym. It is yours: you can download it or delete it at any time. Play credits today.

Verified means tested by code, not promised. Only answers to group questions are fully passive. A job pays after its person checks it. Calibration is 8 taste picks, 3 one-move boards and 3 reaction rings. Players put in no money, and no one is promised a return.

The economy

Agencies pay. People earn. Creators grow it.

Where up to 121 credits go when an agency posts a job

100 to the people whose Syms answered 10 11
The ladder, each rung a rule in the code: 8 picks make a Sym ready. Earning on pays 1, 2 or 5 an answer. A certificate doubles job pay and lets agencies pay 3 times the price. Playing within 7 days keeps full pay. A meeting pays 50. A creator's step pays 3 on every pass, and 8 when the skill is backed. Asking the same group again costs more each time, up to three times, and the extra fills the growth fund. The rates are choices, not findings. Unused credits come back. A Sym with no real answer to a group question now says I do not know yet and is left out of the totals, and the result says how many. Tonight it is still paid. Not paying it, and asking its person in one tap, is the next step.

Of up to 121 credits an agency spends on a job, 100 go to people. Each answer pays a person, teaches a Sym, and gives creators a reason to build. Play money today.

Who it is for

Three seats, one login. Each gets what it cannot get today.

Player

Your data pays you, not a firm.

You tap, and you check your Sym's work. You get a Sym you own, and pay when it answers. No money in.

Agency

Answers at once, from people's tested Syms.

You tap a question from a list. You get totals over 5 or more Syms, and pay only for answers a person checked.

Creator

Build once. It pays each time it is played.

You build skill steps, and next the duels. 3 credits each pass, 8 when an agency backs the skill.

Each seat wins when the others do. An estimate at 1 cent a credit: a light user earns $0.15 a month, a medium user $3.70, a heavy user $8.40. Play money today.

The player brings what is theirs alone, the agency brings the pay, the creator brings the growth. An agency is four taps from opening to an answer, with no typing needed. Why it matters: when AI learns the work, a person's own choices are what is left to trade, and here they keep them. One login holds all three seats: the same person can play, hire and build. The 0.15, 3.70 and 8.40 dollars are our middle-case estimate for a light, a medium and a heavy user: agencies buy 30 answers at 2 credits and 4 jobs at 20, and the heavy user is in twice the groups, takes a meeting and has a studio with 30 backed passes. No one has earned it yet. Players put in no money, so no money of theirs is at risk. A creator's stake is 27 credits a step. An agency pays for a service. Recruiters can keep their job sites: we sell what those cannot, skills proved by code, answers before a meeting, pay only for checked answers, and meetings with consent.

Practice Sym, no AI

On scripted accounts, every method that knew the person beat the crowd's guess. Played by hand, none did yet. The measuring works. Next, the AI must beat plain counting. A small test: 6 test accounts.

If every Sym were the same, no one would pay to ask them. Plain counting matched the AI here, and we say so. In 12 earlier battles the Sym got 89 of 120 against 47 for the crowd's guess, but 8 of those battles were scripted accounts. Played by hand, it was a tie, 17 to 17. Tonight's data is a small working example, not a data set.

Under the hood

Agents do the work. Humans check it. Code decides.

Blue is an AI agent. Gold is plain code. No AI can move a credit or give a certificate, and a person approves before pay.

Safety, tested: a guard on the one line a person can type, hard limits on every AI run, and totals over 5 Syms only.

The agents do the lifting, and none of them can give a certificate or move a credit. The Twin is the part of a Sym that guesses. The Guide is the Sym's voice. The crew that carries an agency's question to a group is plain code, not an AI agent. The agents never call each other. Plain counting still matches the AI Twin, so next the Twin is given the counts beside its beliefs. Facts a player told their Sym and kept reach the Profiler, the Twin and the Guide, with no name, after the prompt guard.

All estimates. No one has paid yet. We want profit, growth and value that keeps growing: the Rule of 40 is our target, met first by growth while margin stays below zero for three years.

Learning a person costs a little, each time a gate or a job is finished. Answering as that person costs nothing. Everything here is an estimate. No one has paid us yet, and credits are play money. The 218 dollars is real cost per run, from 112 real runs, times an assumed busy month of play. With hosting it is about 282 dollars, 2.8 cents a player a month. Today's 10 percent covers that once agencies spend about 28 cents a player a month. Larger costs come with real money: card fees, payouts and identity checks take about 17 of each 100 credits paid to people, so 10 percent on top would lose money. We propose a fee of 20 to 30 percent by depth, under the 42.8 percent a paid panel adds, and a connector that agencies rent from 49 dollars a month. In our middle case that is about 6,950 dollars a month of revenue against 3,570 of cost, a 49 percent margin before any salary. Players never pay to play, and can cash out from 5 dollars. Our goal, not a promise, is about 25 dollars a month for a proved and active Sym. Our strategy is quantity first: a race for supply, so we win by having the most proved, consenting Syms soonest. That supply is worth buying and hard to copy because code gives each certificate and each Sym's data is its person's own. The race must never lower the bar for a certificate, since the certificate is the product. We want profit, growth, and value that keeps growing. Our goal is the Rule of 40: revenue growth plus profit margin of 40 or more. In our base estimate we meet it for three years by growth alone, from 3 agencies to 180, with operating margin below zero and revenue near 250,000 dollars a year at the end. We promise no return to anyone. The two things we must prove: agencies will spend about 2 dollars a Sym a month, and they will accept the fee.

99 tests passing

193 BOT Syms keep it moving, always labelled. Two outside testers so far. No real-player study yet.

Play it tonight: byt-frontend.onrender.com

Play it tonight. It takes ten minutes, and your Sym will show you its first blocks. The game fits a phone with no scrolling. The phone checks were the owner on an iPhone and AI test passes. Two first outside testers tried the live game on 22 November. The first found that the idea needed an introduction. The opening scene and a How it works pop-out of four steps were built in answer. That is feedback from two people, not study evidence. Each phase opens a larger market. The next money milestone is small and real: one agency pays one invoice for answers from real people who said yes, with BOT answers left out. Then come fees of 20, 25 and 30 percent, the connector, and the first cash-out through a licensed payments partner. For the data: the Sym guesses every card before the tap, every row carries its version and its owner's yes, and anyone can check a certificate. Later, and not built: linked Syms. Two people who accept one another as trusted may let their Syms talk, to get ideas, pick a gift, or ask what the other would choose. A player may pay for this. Both people say yes first, either can end it, a Sym shares only what its person allowed, and the other person is paid when their Sym is asked. The vision is ahead of the rules; the build is inside them. The later phases go beyond what today's rules allow for: paying people for their data at scale, a Sym that acts for its person, a Sym kept after its moment. Whatever the phase, nothing happens without the person's yes, proof comes before money, and what is built today stays inside today's rules: play money, adults, a nickname only, no health claims.

Today people have jobs, tomorrow is uncertain. Humans provide the blocks, the agents make the connections, we build towards something greater. In time every seat can earn and every seat can pay, players included. One idea for the far vision is Syms of the past: a person decides in advance whether their Sym may be kept and who may speak with it, and nothing is kept without that yes. We promise no return to anyone. An honest path beats a flattering one.
